original_value: Detection and distance measurement using sensors is not always accurate. Sensor fusion makes up for this shortcoming by reducing inaccuracies. This study, therefore, proposes an extended Kalman filter (EKF) that reflects the distance characteristics of lidar and radar sensors. The sensor characteristics of the lidar and radar over distance were analyzed, and a reliability function was designed to extend the Kalman filter to reflect distance characteristics. The accuracy of position estimation was improved by identifying the sensor errors according to distance. Experiments were conducted using real vehicles, and a comparative experiment was done combining sensor fusion using a fuzzy, adaptive measure noise and Kalman filter. Experimental results showed that the study’s method produced accurate distance estimations.

result.paraphrase: Sensor-based detection and distance measurement are not always precise. Sensor fusion can compensate for this limitation by reducing errors. Accordingly, this study proposes an extended Kalman filter (EKF) that captures the distance-dependent characteristics of lidar and radar sensors. The distance-based sensor behavior of lidar and radar was analyzed, and a reliability function was developed to extend the Kalman filter so it reflects those distance characteristics. By identifying sensor errors according to distance, position-estimation accuracy was improved. Experiments were performed with real vehicles, and a comparative test combined sensor fusion with a fuzzy adaptive measurement noise and Kalman filter. The results showed that the proposed method achieved accurate distance estimation.
